newsitem.title: USA: Clinton proposes new regulation for child seats.
newsitem.headline: Clinton proposes new regulation for child seats.

text.p: President Bill Clinton proposed on Saturday that the federal government require automobile manufacturers to include in new vehicles a universal system for attaching child safety seats.

"This system, developed by a blue-ribbon commission of industry and consumer groups, will make safety seats easier to install and more secure on the road. It will save young lives," Clinton said in his weekly radio address, taped on Friday for Saturday broadcast.
Under the proposal put forward by the Transportation Department, every new car would be equipped with standard latches in the back seat designed specifically to fasten to these buckles.
There would also be universal attachments to secure the top of the safety seat to the car's interior, so car seats would be locked in from top to bottom.
The idea emerged from a blue-ribbon panel of experts put together by the Transportation Department to address problems with child safety seat installation and use.

A White House fact sheet said not all 100 models of safety seats available fit in all 900 passenger vehicle models, so as a result an estimated 80 percent of parents fail to properly secure children in seats or fully attach seats to vehicles.
Clinton said the proposal would go out for public comment next week and if approved, the new safety system could be on the market by 1999.
"With this plan, we're moving closer to the day when safe, well-attached car seats will be the rule of the road," he said.

The White House said the proposal would be expected to save dozens of lives and prevent thousands of injuries annually of children four years old and younger. It is also expected to increase safety seat use by reducing consumer frustration.
